best_for: Data analysts and researchers on Windows or a Mac who work in R or Python and want an editor with a console, data viewer and plots built in, rather than a general code editor they have to assemble from extensions.
description:
Positron is a free IDE for data science from Posit Software, PBC, the company behind RStudio, the tidyverse and Shiny.

The Posit Assistant is an AI helper that connects to your live Python or R session, so it sees your actual data when it helps you explore, plot or debug. You can move between a notebook and a console that keeps several sessions open. The Data Explorer lets you explore and reshape large datasets, on your machine or remote. When your analysis turns into an app, API, notebook or report, you can preview it in Positron and publish it with guided steps.

points.title: Free to use, with one licence catch
points.text: Positron is source-available under the Elastic License 2.0. Posit allows personal, academic and commercial use, but you may not offer it to others as a hosted or managed service without Posit's agreement. A separate education rider permits hosting for courses when only enrolled students and staff get access. The ark R kernel and the air formatter it uses are MIT.

points.title: R, Python and SQL are the core languages
points.text: Posit treats R, Python and SQL as first-class, with SQL needing the ggsql extension. Other languages come through extensions, such as a community Julia one, and languages like Rust or C++ work without the data tools. Positron starts with no language installed, Python can be installed for you, and R must be 4.2 or newer.

points.title: Built on Code OSS, so VS Code extensions mostly fit
points.text: Positron is built on Code OSS, the open base of VS Code, and installs VS Code-compatible extensions, including .vsix files. Posit made a separate app because the VS Code extension API cannot reshape the main workbench. The desktop app can also work over remote SSH sessions.

points.title: RStudio stays alongside it
points.text: Posit says it keeps maintaining and updating RStudio. Large new features go to Positron first, while RStudio gets security, stability and targeted fixes, so moving is a choice rather than a forced migration.

points.title: Per-user or machine-wide on Windows
points.text: This listing carries two x64 Inno Setup installers for each release: a user setup that installs for your account only and a system setup that installs for the whole machine. Posit asks for Windows 10 or later and the latest Visual C++ Redistributable. Rtools is not bundled, which matters only for some R package building.

points.title: Arm64 Windows and Linux are not listed here
points.text: Posit also publishes an Arm64 build for Windows 11 and Linux packages for x64 and Arm64: .deb for Ubuntu 20 or later and Debian, and .rpm for RHEL 9 and Fedora. This listing covers x64 Windows and macOS, where the Intel and Apple silicon builds come as separate zip files.

points.title: Older builds are kept for Windows only
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 36 versions, going back to 2024.07.0. macOS shows only the current release, so an older Mac build needs another source.
